title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis Protocol
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7q7hmzn

steps.title: Prepare agarose solution
steps.instruction: Gather a 250 mL flask and a 250 mL measuring cylinder; add 1 g agarose to the flask, then add 130 mL TAE using the measuring cylinder, tape the container, and place a comb inside.

steps.title: Melt agarose
steps.instruction: Microwave the flask containing agarose and TAE for 1 minute. If the solution is not homogeneous, continue microwaving in 15‑second increments until it becomes clear and uniform.

steps.title: Add ethidium bromide and pour gel
steps.instruction: Transfer the hot (quasi‑boiling) agarose solution, still in its taped and combed container, to the cold room; add 1 µL ethidium bromide to the solution, then carefully pour it into the container, avoiding any spillage. If spillage occurs, stop, clean the mess, and start the pour again.

steps.title: Clean the flask
steps.instruction: Add a small amount of water to the flask, rinse thoroughly, and dispose of the contaminated water in the liquid EtBr waste via the designated white container. Then wash the flask with water and place it in the dirty‑dishes trolley.

steps.title: Solidify gel
steps.instruction: Leave the poured gel to solidify in the cold room. If the gel will be used the next day, wrap it in a plastic sheet to prevent desiccation.

steps.title: Set up gel in electrophoresis tank
steps.instruction: Remove the tape from the solidified gel, place the gel into the electrophoresis tank, and add 5 µL DNA ladder to the appropriate well.

steps.title: Prepare and load DNA samples
steps.instruction: Mix 2 µL loading buffer with 5 µL DNA sample (approximately 100 ng) and load the mixture into the designated wells of the gel.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Connect the electrophoresis tank cables to the Bio‑Rad power supply, set the program to 150 V, 400 mA for 30 minutes, and start the run.

steps.title: Monitor and image gel
steps.instruction: Check the gel every 10 minutes. After the run, place the gel in the imager, open Image Lab, create a new protocol, position the gel, adjust zoom, start the imaging protocol, then invert and adjust contrast as needed and print the image. Handle the computer with gloves as it is considered contaminated.
